title: Keyset pagination over an org's user directory
name: User directory listing

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code paginates through an organization's users? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does the query request limit + 1 rows?
choices: To include the cursor row itself so the client can confirm continuity
To know whether another page exists without running a separate COUNT query
To compensate for rows filtered out by the status condition after fetching
Because Postgres LIMIT is exclusive of its bound

questions.prompt: A new user is inserted into the org while a client is halfway through paging. Assuming created_at is the insertion time, what does the client see?
choices: The new user appears on the next page, shifting every later row by one
A user from the previous page is repeated on the next page
Pages already fetched are unaffected and the new user does not appear in the remaining pages
The cursor becomes invalid and the next request fails

questions.prompt: A client sends a cursor that is valid base64url but decodes to {"createdAt":"x"}. What happens in listUsers?
choices: The cursor is ignored and the first page is returned
The query runs with a null id and returns nothing
Postgres raises a cast error that propagates to the caller
